parsed.why: Decriminalised conduct and no trans-specific offence, but no hate-crime or anti-discrimination recourse, official calls to exile trans people, gay-panic judicial leniency, and an LGBT visitor beaten at carnival: hostile society, thin remedy.

Penal code criminalises same-sex relations; presidential decree frames LGBTQ people as defence threats; mobs attack trans women; police raid venues; a trans traveller died in custody after extortion demands. State-directed organised targeting.

No criminalisation and paper protections (anti-discrimination law, hate-crime provision, custody search protocol), but enforcement weak: unsanctioned police torture of LGBT people, 20+ unpunished attacks on an LGBT centre, hostile public.

Decriminalised by 2022 court ruling that read sex discrimination to cover gender identity; no documented trans targeting, violence or police practice, though statutory protections and hate-crime recourse remain absent.

No criminalisation, entrenched third-gender recognition, education and community infrastructure, but documented street harassment and violence against visibly trans people plus rising political hostility; latent 'unnatural sex' statute remains on the books.
